ordered_diagnoses: Inflammatory Myopathy associated with Anti-Synthetase Syndrome

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive proximal muscle weakness with inflammatory and autoimmune features
salient_findings: Progressive proximal muscle weakness over 2 months
Morning stiffness of small hand joints
key_facts: 14-year-old girl presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness
Difficulty combing hair and rising from a chair
Morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
Poor appetite without fever or weight loss
Symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in upper limbs and 3/5 in lower limbs
Brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Suppressed TSH and elevated free T4

shortlist: Inflammatory Myopathy associated with Anti-Synthetase Syndrome

shortlist.label: Juvenile Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and skin findings are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis with Myositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of thyroiditis, current thyroid function tests, and presence of anti-thyroglobulin antibodies support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Inflammatory Myopathy associated with Anti-Synthetase Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory markers, muscle weakness, and presence of anti-thyroglobulin antibodies are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis-Sine-Dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive proximal muscle weakness and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with this diagnosis, despite lack of skin findings

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and absence of skin findings are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis. The presence of leukopenia, microcytic anemia, and elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies also support this diagnosis. Although the patient has a history of thyroiditis, the current presentation and laboratory findings are more suggestive of Juvenile Dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis with Myositis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of thyroiditis and elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies, the primary presentation is muscle weakness and inflammatory markers, which is more consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Inflammatory Myopathy associated with Anti-Synthetase Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of anti-synthetase antibodies or other specific features of this syndrome, making it less likely.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis-Sine-Dermatitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis, and there is no indication that the skin manifestations are absent.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's age and presentation are more consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis, and polymyositis is typically seen in adults.
